segments.md:
# The Declare model, a screen at a time

A tour of how Declare puts things on the screen: views, constraints, layout,
paint, transforms and effects, composition, data, and layouts of your own. Each
screen makes one point, shows the code that makes it, and shows it happening on
a stage every screen shares, so one screen turns into the next in front of the
reader.

How it is built:

- **The screens are data**, `steps.json`: each one's title, its point, its code,
  its geometry and its controls. The code carries slots (`{{w}}`) filled from the
  screen's geometry and the reader's choices, so the numbers in the code are the
  numbers on the stage, and dragging the box rewrites its `x`.
- **Where the reader is** is `location`, the URL's fragment: one screen's id. The
  contents, Back and Next, and the arrow keys all write it; Back in the browser
  undoes it. **What the reader has chosen** — where the box was dragged, the axis,
  the padding — is one record, `choices`, which every control writes and the stage
  reads.
- **The stage** is in `stage.declare`: one cast of views, posed for each screen
  by a `Director` and carried between poses on springs.
- **The code panel moves too.** Its lines are records with identities: lines that
  stay slide to their new places, new ones open, lines that leave fold away, and
  the lines a screen adds to the one before it are lit.

include [ "stage.declare" ]

// ── Helpers ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
//
// Plain functions of their arguments: a line of code as colored runs.

script {
    function esc(s: string): string {
        return s.replace(/&/g, "&").replace(/</g, "<").replace(/>/g, ">").replace(/ /g, " ")
    }

    // A line of Declare as HTML runs, one style per kind of token.
    function colored(line: string): string {
        const re = /(\/\/.*$)|(\x22(?:[^\x22\\]|\\.)*\x22)|(\b(?:class|extends|const|return|let|true|false)\b)|(\b[A-Z][A-Za-z0-9]*\b)|(0x[0-9A-Fa-f]+|#[0-9A-Fa-f]{6,8}\b|\b\d+(?:\.\d+)?%?)|([\[\]{}])/g
        const kinds = ["Comment", "StringText", "Keyword", "TypeName", "NumberText", "Punctuation"]
        let out = "", last = 0
        let m: RegExpExecArray | null
        while ((m = re.exec(line)) != null) {
            const kind = kinds[[m[1], m[2], m[3], m[4], m[5], m[6]].findIndex((g) => g !== undefined)]
            out += esc(line.slice(last, m.index)) + "<span class='" + kind + "'>" + esc(m[0]) + "</span>"
            last = re.lastIndex
        }
        return out + esc(line.slice(last))
    }

    // The appearance the page that sent the reader here was wearing, when its
    // link said (`?appearance=dark` or `light`); "auto" otherwise, and where there
    // is no address (the Mac app).
    function requestedAppearance(): string {
        const location = (globalThis as { location?: { search: string } }).location
        const m = location?.search.match(/[?&]appearance=(light|dark)\b/)
        return m != null ? m[1] : "auto"
    }
    }


// ── The shape of the data ───────────────────────────────────────────────────

schema Part [ id: string, name: string ]
schema Choice [ id: string, label: string ]

// A control a screen offers: a choice among `items`, a number from `min` to
// `max`, a toggle (`label` while off, `labelOn` while on), or a verb on the
// stage's records. `name` is the choice it writes, or the verb.

schema Knob [ kind: "segmented" | "slider" | "toggle" | "verb", name: string, label: string,
    labelOn?: string, items[]?: Choice, min?: number, max?: number, step?: number ]

// A screen. `live` says what its chips do when pressed (they count presses, or
// toggle), and `drag` that the box itself is dragged. `core` is its place in the
// ten minutes; a screen without one comes after them, in the order of the file.

schema Step [ id: string, part: string, title: string, point: string, hint: string, code[]: string,
    geo?: Geo, knobs[]: Knob, live?: "press" | "toggle", drag?: boolean, core?: number ]

// The colors the lessons' programs give a panel and a light box — the code says
// them and the stage paints them, read with Color.from — one pair for a light
// page, one for a dark.

schema Paint [ panel: string, box: string ]
schema Tour [ parts[]: Part, chip: ChipGeo, paint: [ light: Paint, dark: Paint ], steps[]: Step ]

// What the reader has chosen, screen by screen.

schema Choices [ dx: number, dy: number, words: string, swapped: boolean, panelWidth: number,
    size: number, open: boolean, axis: "y" | "x", align: "start" | "center" | "end", rowWidth: number,
    padding: number, fill: "color" | "gradient", sides: "all" | "bottom", corners: "one" | "four" | "pill",
    lift: number, presence: "shown" | "faded" | "clear" | "hidden", done: number,
    clip: "none" | "box" | "shape", scaleBy: number, turn: number, pivot: "middle" | "corner",
    filter: "none" | "blur" | "grayscale" | "hue", frost: boolean, label: string, status: "doing" | "done",
    round: boolean ]

// The data screens' records, and a line of the code panel: its text and its
// identity, then whether it is leaving and whether this screen added it.

schema Item [ id: number, label: string, status: "doing" | "done" ]
schema SourceLine [ id: string, text: string ]
schema CodeRow [ id: string, text: string, gone: boolean, fresh: boolean ]

// A quiet control: smaller, its "on" and its edge greys rather than the tour's ink
// (the "Show boxes" switch, which is an aid, not part of the lesson).

theme QuietLight [ accent = #A3ABB8, line = #D5DAE1, trackFill = #E6E9EE,
    switchWidth = 32, switchHeight = 18, switchThumbOffSize = 14
    ]


theme QuietDark [ accent = #5D6573, line = #343A45, trackFill = #2A2F38, switchThumbFill = #A3ABB8,
    switchWidth = 32, switchHeight = 18, switchThumbOffSize = 14
    ]


// the code's colors, one per kind of token (`colored`, above, names them), for a
// light page and for a dark one

style Keyword [ textColor = #8250DF ]

style TypeName [ textColor = #0B5FBF ]

style StringText [ textColor = #0A7D45 ]

style NumberText [ textColor = #B35400 ]

style Comment [ textColor = #6E7781, italic = true ]

style Punctuation [ textColor = #6E7781 ]

style PunctuationOnDark [ textColor = #89DDFF ]

// ── The records ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

// The data screens' records, and every write to them: the verbs the change
// screen's code shows, each a button there.

class Records extends Dataset [ schema = [ rows[]: Item ],
    all() -> Item[] { return this.read(["rows"]) ?? [] },
    nextLabel() -> string? { return app.labels.find((l) => !this.all().some((r) => r.label == l)) ?? null },
    can(verb: string) -> boolean {
        switch (verb) {
            case "insert": return this.nextLabel() != null
            case "remove": return this.all().length > 1
            default: return this.all().length >= 3
            }
        },
    run(verb: string) {
        const label = this.nextLabel()
        if (!this.can(verb)) return
        if (verb == "insert" && label != null) {
            const id = this.all().reduce((m, r) => Math.max(m, r.id), 0) + 1
            this.insert(["rows"], 0, ({ id: id, label: label, status: "doing" }))
        }
        if (verb == "remove") this.removeAt(["rows"], 0)
        if (verb == "move") this.move(["rows"], 0, 2)
        }
    ]


// ── The code panel's model ──────────────────────────────────────────────────

class Listing extends Node [

    // A screen's code with its slots filled. A line keeps its identity while
    // its numbers change, so its id is its unfilled text; a line that is all
    // slot is known by what fills it. Repeated lines are told apart by count.

    lines(id: string) -> SourceLine[] {
        const s = app.steps.find((x) => x.id == id)
        if (s == null) return []
        const seen = new Map<string, number>()
        const out: SourceLine[] = []
        for (const t of s.code) {
            const filled = t.replace(/\{\{(\w+)\}\}/g, (_m: string, k: string) => this.slot(id, k))
            const whole = /^\{\{\w+\}\}$/.test(t)
            for (const line of filled.split("\n")) {
                const key = whole ? line.replace(/,$/, "") : t
                const n = (seen.get(key) ?? 0) + 1
                seen.set(key, n)
                out.push(({ id: key + "#" + n, text: line }))
            }
        }
        return out
        },

    // What fills a slot: the reader's choice where the screen offers one, else
    // the screen's geometry, else the chip's.

    slot(id: string, key: string) -> string {
        const c = app.choices.value
        const g = app.director.geo(id)
        const drag = app.steps.find((s) => s.id == id)?.drag ?? false
        switch (key) {
            case "x": return "" + ((g.x ?? 0) + (drag ? c.dx : 0))
            case "y": return "" + ((g.y ?? 0) + (drag ? c.dy : 0))
            case "w": {
                const k = app.widthKnob(id)
                return "" + (k != null ? app.widthOf(k.name) : g.w ?? 0)
                }
            case "words": return c.words
            case "first": return this.child(c.swapped ? "b" : "a", g) + ","
            case "second": return this.child(c.swapped ? "a" : "b", g)
            case "clipLine": return this.clipLine(c.clip)
            case "size": return "" + c.size
            case "open": return "" + c.open
            case "axis": return c.axis
            case "align": return c.align
            case "padding": return "" + c.padding
            case "fill": return c.fill == "color" ? "steelblue" : "{ Gradient.linear(\"135deg\", 0x3B82F6, 0x8B5CF6) }"
            case "stroke": return c.sides == "all" ? "{ Stroke(4, 0x3B82F6) }" : "{ [null, null, Stroke(4, 0x3B82F6), null] }"
            case "corners": return this.cornersText(c.corners)
            case "dy": return "" + Math.round(2 + 14 * c.lift)
            case "blur": return "" + Math.round(4 + 36 * c.lift)
            case "presence": return this.presenceText(c.presence)
            case "done": return c.done.toFixed(2)
            case "turn": return "" + c.turn
            case "px": return c.pivot == "middle" ? "" + (g.w ?? 0) / 2 : "0"
            case "py": return c.pivot == "middle" ? "" + (g.h ?? 0) / 2 : "0"
            case "halfW": return "" + (g.w ?? 0) / 2
            case "halfH": return "" + (g.h ?? 0) / 2
            case "scaleBy": return c.scaleBy.toFixed(1)
            case "filter": return this.filterText(c.filter)
            case "frost": return c.frost ? "{ VisualFilter.frost(14) }" : "null"
            case "panelFill": return app.paint.panel
            case "boxFill": return app.paint.box
            case "label": return c.label
            case "status": return c.status
            default: {
                const v = g[key as keyof Geo] ?? app.director.chipGeo[key as keyof ChipGeo]
                return v == null ? "" : "" + v
                }
            }
        },
    child(name: string, g: Geo) -> string {
        const a = name == "a"
        const box = a ? [g.ax, g.ay, g.aw, g.ah] : [g.bx, g.by, g.bw, g.bh]
        return `    ${name}: View [ x = ${box[0]}, y = ${box[1]}, width = ${box[2]}, height = ${box[3]},\n        fill = ${a ? "steelblue" : "teal"} ]`
        },
    clipLine(m: string) -> string {
        if (m == "none") return "    // no clip: children paint past the edge"
        if (m == "box") return "    clip = true,"
        return "    clip = \"" + app.director.clipShape(360, 280).split(" L ").slice(0, 3).join(" L ") + " …\","
        },
    cornersText(m: string) -> string {
        if (m == "four") return "[48, 0, 48, 0]"
        return m == "pill" ? "80" : "24"
        },
    presenceText(m: string) -> string {
        switch (m) {
            case "faded": return "opacity = 0.25"
            case "clear": return "opacity = 0"
            case "hidden": return "visible = false"
            default: return "opacity = 1"
            }
        },
    filterText(m: string) -> string {
        switch (m) {
            case "blur": return "{ VisualFilter.blur(4) }"
            case "grayscale": return "{ VisualFilter.grayscale(1) }"
            case "hue": return "{ VisualFilter.hueRotate(120) }"
            default: return "null"
            }
        },

    // What the panel shows: the current lines in order, and the lines leaving,
    // each where it stood. A line is lit when this screen adds it to the code of
    // the screen before — so only where the two share code: a screen whose code
    // is all new has nothing added, and lights nothing.

    merged(prev: SourceLine[], cur: SourceLine[], before: SourceLine[]) -> CodeRow[] {
        const has = new Set(cur.map((r) => r.id))
        const had = new Set(before.map((r) => r.id))
        // (a line of brackets alone is shared by every screen, and says nothing)
        const builds = cur.some((r) => had.has(r.id) && /\w/.test(r.text))
        const out: CodeRow[] = cur.map((r) => ({ id: r.id, text: r.text, gone: false, fresh: builds && !had.has(r.id) }))
        let anchor = -1
        prev.forEach((r) => {
            if (has.has(r.id)) { anchor = out.findIndex((o) => o.id == r.id); return }
            anchor = anchor + 1
            out.splice(anchor, 0, ({ id: r.id, text: r.text, gone: true, fresh: false }))
            })
        return out
        }
    ]


// A line of code. A new line opens from nothing and a leaving one folds to
// nothing, each on a spring on its own height; the panel stacks them, so the
// lines between slide as they do.

class CodeLine [ width = 100%, clip = true,
    gone: boolean = { :gone ?? false },
    fresh: boolean = { :fresh ?? false },
    height = 0,
    opacity = 0,
    visible = { this.height > 0.5 || !classroot.gone },
    Glide [ attribute = height, to = { classroot.gone ? 0 : 22 } ],
    Glide [ attribute = opacity, to = { classroot.gone ? 0 : 1 } ],
    litT: number = 0,
    Glide [ attribute = litT, to = { classroot.fresh && !classroot.gone ? 1 : 0 } ],
    lit: View [ width = 100%, height = 100%, fill = { provided("theme").codeFreshFill }, opacity = { classroot.litT } ],
    bar: View [ width = 3, height = 100%, fill = { provided("theme").noteInk }, opacity = { classroot.litT } ],
    HTMLText [ x = 16, y = 4, fontSize = 12, fontFamily = { app.monoFace },
        bodyColor = { provided("theme").codeTextColor }, html = { colored(:text ?? "") } ]
    ]


// ── The screen's controls ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
//
// Each is a record of the screen's (`knobs`), built as the class its kind names.
// The class reads its record — which choice, its labels, its range — and the
// control inside it sits on the reader's choices and edits the one it names:
// `:@[(classroot.choice)]` is that field, both ways.

// (A Segmented is rooted on its own segments, so the field is held around it.)

class ChoiceSegments [
    choice: string = { :name ?? "" },
    options: Choice[] = { :items ?? [] },
    View [ datapath = { app.choices.value },
        picked: string = { "" + :@[(classroot.choice)] },
        pick(v: string) { :@[(classroot.choice)] = v },
        Segmented [ segmentWidths = "proportional", items = { classroot.options }, value = { parent.picked },
            commit(v: string) { parent.pick(v) }
            ]
        ]
    ]


class ChoiceSlider [
    choice: string = { :name ?? "" },
    Slider [ width = 160, height = { app.target }, datapath = { app.choices.value },
        min = { parent.min }, max = { parent.max }, step = { parent.step },
        accessibilityLabel = { parent.label },
        value <-> { :@[(classroot.choice)] } ],
    min: number = { :min ?? 0 },
    max: number = { :max ?? 1 },
    step: number = { :step ?? 0.1 },
    label: string = { :label ?? "" }
    ]


class ChoiceToggle [
    choice: string = { :name ?? "" },
    label: string = { :label ?? "" },
    labelOn: string = { :labelOn ?? :label ?? "" },
    Button [ datapath = { app.choices.value },
        on: boolean = { :@[(classroot.choice)] == true },
        accessibilityPressed = { this.on },
        label = { this.on ? classroot.labelOn : classroot.label },
        onClick() { :@[(classroot.choice)] = !on }
        ]
    ]


class RecordVerb extends Button [
    verb: string = { :name ?? "" },
    label = { :label ?? "" },
    disabled = { !app.records.can(classroot.verb) },
    onClick() { app.records.run(verb) }
    ]


// ── The tour's own controls ─────────────────────────────────────────────────

// The contents' mark, drawn as the library's icons are, on a 16-unit grid: a
// list.

class ListIcon extends Icon [
    draw(d: DrawContext) {
        d.scale(unit, unit)
        d.strokeStyle = ink
        d.lineWidth = weight / unit
        d.lineCap = "round"
        d.beginPath()
        for (const y of [4, 8, 12]) { d.moveTo(2.5, y); d.lineTo(3, y); d.moveTo(6, y); d.lineTo(13.5, y) }
        d.stroke()
        }
    ]


// A square button that is only its icon: its name is said by a screen reader
// and shown on hover.

class IconButton extends Control [ width = { app.target }, height = { app.target }, cornerRadius = 8,
    ink: Color = { provided("theme").textMuted },
    accessibilityLabel = { this.tooltipLabel },
    fill = { pressed ? provided("theme").quietFillPressed : hovered ? provided("theme").quietFillHovered : null }
    ]


class ContentsButton extends IconButton [ tooltipLabel = "Contents",
    ListIcon [ x = center, y = center, iconSize = 16, ink = { classroot.ink } ]
    ]


// Back: Next's pill, mirrored, without its fill, since going back is the
// exception — the accent's ink alone.

class BackLink extends Control [ height = { app.touchFirst ? 44 : 40 }, cornerRadius = { this.height / 2 }, padding = [0, 18, 0, 14],
    accessibilityLabel = { "Back: " + (app.steps[app.index - 1]?.title ?? "") },
    tooltipLabel = { app.steps[app.index - 1]?.title ?? "" },
    fill = { pressed ? provided("theme").quietFillPressed : hovered ? provided("theme").quietFillHovered : null },
    State [ applied = { classroot.disabled }, opacity = 0 ],
    layout: SimpleLayout [ axis = x, spacing = 6, align = center ],
    ChevronIcon [ dir = "left", iconSize = 16, ink = { provided("theme").accent } ],
    Text [ fontSize = 14, fontWeight = semibold, textColor = { provided("theme").accent }, text = "Back" ]
    ]


// Next: the way a reader goes, in the tour's ink, named for where it leads —
// on a narrow page, only "Next".

class NextPill extends Control [ height = { app.touchFirst ? 44 : 40 }, cornerRadius = { this.height / 2 }, padding = [0, 14, 0, 18],
    title: string = "",
    accessibilityLabel = { "Next: " + classroot.title },
    fill = { pressed ? provided("theme").accentPressed : hovered ? provided("theme").accentHovered : provided("theme").accent },
    State [ applied = { classroot.disabled }, opacity = { provided("theme").disabledOpacity } ],
    layout: SimpleLayout [ axis = x, spacing = 6, align = center ],
    Text [ fontSize = 14, fontWeight = semibold, wrap = false, textColor = { provided("theme").accentTextColor },
        text = { app.compact ? "Next" : "Next: " + classroot.title } ],
    ChevronIcon [ dir = "right", iconSize = 16, ink = { provided("theme").accentTextColor } ]
    ]


// ── Where the reader is ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────

// The way through the tour, a tick for each screen: the ten minutes, then the
// screens going further, quieter and apart. The screens read are tinted, the one
// shown is lit, and each tick is a link to its screen.

// (Too small for a finger: on a touch device the ticks only show the way, and
// Back, Next and the contents move along it.)

class Tick extends Control [ flexes = true, height = 24, focusable = false, disabled = { app.touchFirst },
    id: string = { :id ?? "" },
    here: boolean = { app.stepId == classroot.id },
    read: boolean = { classroot.rowIndex < app.index },
    further: boolean = { :core == null },
    startsFurther: boolean = { classroot.further && app.steps[classroot.rowIndex - 1]?.core != null },
    State [ applied = { classroot.startsFurther }, padding = [0, 0, 0, 14] ],
    State [ applied = { classroot.further && !classroot.here }, opacity = 0.6 ],
    link = { "#" + classroot.id },
    tooltipLabel = { :title ?? "" },
    bar: View [ width = 100%, y = center, cornerRadius = 2,
        height = { classroot.here ? 6 : classroot.hovered ? 5 : 3 },
        fill = { classroot.here ? provided("theme").accent : classroot.read ? provided("theme").tickVisitedFill : provided("theme").tickFill } ]
    ]


class Progress [ datapath = { app.route.value },
    layout: SimpleLayout [ axis = y, spacing = 2, align = center ],
    ticks: View [ width = 100%, visible = { !app.narrow },
        layout: SimpleLayout [ axis = x, spacing = 2, align = center ],
        Tick [ datapath = :steps[] ]
        ],

    // (where the contents are hidden, the bar above the title says this)

    Text [ visible = { app.wide }, fontSize = 12, textColor = { provided("theme").textFaint },
        text = { app.whereIs(app.index) } ]
    ]


// ── The contents ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

// A screen in the contents: its number and title, a link to it — under its
// part's name, when it is the part's first screen.

class RailStep [ width = 100%,
    id: string = { :id ?? "" },
    here: boolean = { app.stepId == classroot.id },
    inCore: boolean = { :core != null },
    startsRoute: boolean = { rowIndex == 0 || (!classroot.inCore && app.steps[rowIndex - 1]?.core != null) },
    startsPart: boolean = { !classroot.inCore && (classroot.startsRoute || app.steps[rowIndex - 1]?.part != :part) },
    layout: SimpleLayout [ axis = y ],
    Text [ exists = { classroot.startsRoute }, padding = [18, 12, 4, 12], fontSize = 13, fontWeight = semibold,
        text = { classroot.inCore ? "Declare in 10 minutes" : "Going further" } ],
    Text [ exists = { classroot.startsPart }, padding = [10, 12, 6, 12], fontSize = 11, fontWeight = semibold,
        letterSpacing = 0.8, textTransform = uppercase, textColor = { provided("theme").textFaint },
        text = { app.partName(:part ?? "") } ],
    row: View [ width = 100%, height = 32, cornerRadius = 8, padding = [0, 12, 0, 12],
        link = { "#" + classroot.id },
        onClick() { app.contentsOpen = false },
        fill = { hovered ? provided("theme").background : null },
        State [ applied = { classroot.here }, fill = { provided("theme").railCurrentFill } ],
        layout: SimpleLayout [ axis = x, spacing = 10, align = center ],
        Text [ width = 18, fontSize = 12, fontFamily = { app.monoFace }, textAlign = end,
            textColor = { classroot.here ? provided("theme").railCurrentTextColor : provided("theme").textFaint }, text = { "" + (classroot.rowIndex + 1) } ],
        Text [ flexes = true, fontSize = 14, wrap = false, maxLines = 1,
            fontWeight = { classroot.here ? "semibold" : "regular" },
            textColor = { classroot.here ? provided("theme").railCurrentTextColor : provided("theme").text }, text = { :title ?? "" } ]
        ]
    ]


class Contents [ width = 100%, datapath = { app.route.value },
    layout: SimpleLayout [ axis = y, spacing = 2 ],
    RailStep [ datapath = :steps[] ]
    ]


// ── The app ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

App [ appName = "The Declare model", minWidth = 360,

    // the appearance: the one the sending page asked for, else the system's,
    // until the reader presses the switch, after which theirs holds

    themeMode: string = { requestedAppearance() },
    isDark: boolean = { app.themeMode == "auto" ? app.systemDark : app.themeMode == "dark" },

    theme = { { ...(app.isDark ? ({ ...SanFranciscoDark, ...TourDark }) : ({ ...SanFrancisco, ...TourLight })),
        ...app.fingerSizes } },

    // on a device built for touch, the stage's controls are a finger's size

    target: number = { app.touchFirst ? 44 : 32 },
    fingerSizes: object = { app.touchFirst
        ? ({ segmentedHeight: 44, segmentedCornerRadius: 22, buttonHeight: 44, buttonCornerRadius: 22,
            switchWidth: 51, switchHeight: 31, switchThumbOffSize: 27 }) : ({}) },
    fill = { provided("theme").background },
    textColor = { provided("theme").text },
    uiFace: string[] = ["-apple-system", "system-ui", "Segoe UI", "Helvetica Neue", "sans-serif"],
    monoFace: string[] = ["ui-monospace", "SFMono-Regular", "Menlo", "monospace"],
    fontFamily = { app.uiFace },
    textStyles = { app.isDark
        ? ({ Keyword: KeywordOnDark, TypeName: TypeNameOnDark, StringText: StringTextOnDark,
            NumberText: NumberTextOnDark, Comment: CommentOnDark, Punctuation: PunctuationOnDark })
        : ({ Keyword, TypeName, StringText, NumberText, Comment, Punctuation }) },

    // ── the screens

    tour: DataSource [ url = "steps.json", autoFetch = true, schema = Tour ],

    // the ten minutes first, in their order; then every other screen, going further

    steps: Step[] = { [
        ...(app.tour.value?.steps ?? []).filter((s) => s.core != null).sort((a, b) => (a.core ?? 0) - (b.core ?? 0)),
        ...(app.tour.value?.steps ?? []).filter((s) => s.core == null) ] },
    route: Dataset [ contents = { { steps: app.steps } } ],
    order: string[] = { app.steps.map((s) => s.id) },
    coreCount: number = { app.steps.filter((s) => s.core != null).length },
    paint: Paint = { (app.isDark ? app.tour.value?.paint.dark : app.tour.value?.paint.light) ?? ({ panel: "whitesmoke", box: "white" }) },
    partName(id: string) -> string { return app.tour.value?.parts.find((p) => p.id == id)?.name ?? "" },

    // where a screen sits: in the ten minutes, by its number; past them, by its part

    whereIs(i: number) -> string {
        const s = app.steps[i]
        if (s == null) return ""
        return s.core != null ? "Declare in 10 minutes  ·  " + (i + 1) + " of " + app.coreCount
            : "Going further  ·  " + app.partName(s.part)
        },

    // ── where the reader is: one screen, named in the URL

    location = "view",
    index: number = { Math.max(0, app.order.indexOf(app.location)) },
    step: Step? = { app.steps[app.index] ?? null },
    stepId: string = { app.step?.id ?? "view" },
    go(i: number) { if (i >= 0 && i < order.length) location = order[i] },
    next() { go(index + 1) },
    back() { go(index - 1) },
    keyBindings = { [ ({ key: "ArrowRight", command: "next", label: "Next screen" }),
        ({ key: "ArrowLeft", command: "back", label: "Previous screen" }) ] },

    // the screen shown before this one, whose notes and code are leaving; a
    // screen is entered with the box where its screen puts it, and its pane at
    // the top

    prevStep: string = "view",
    trackChanges = ["stepId"],
    onChange(e: ChangeEvent) {
        prevStep = e.changed[0].previousValue as string
        choices.set(["dx"], 0)
        choices.set(["dy"], 0)
        app.stage.p.scrollTo(0)
        },

    // ── what the reader has chosen, screen by screen

    choices: Dataset [ schema = Choices ] { {
        "dx": 0, "dy": 0, "words": "Hello, world", "swapped": false, "panelWidth": 360, "size": 60, "open": false,
        "axis": "y", "align": "start", "rowWidth": 460, "padding": 20, "fill": "color", "sides": "all",
        "corners": "one", "lift": 0.5, "presence": "shown", "done": 0.6, "clip": "none", "scaleBy": 0.6,
        "turn": 20, "pivot": "middle", "filter": "none", "frost": false, "label": "Design", "status": "doing",
        "round": true } },

    // the box dragged (or nudged), kept on the stage

    moveBox(dx: number, dy: number) {
        const g = director.geo(stepId), w = g.w ?? 0, h = g.h ?? 0, x = g.x ?? 0, y = g.y ?? 0
        choices.set(["dx"], Math.round(Math.max(10 - x, Math.min(STAGE_W - 10 - w - x, dx))))
        choices.set(["dy"], Math.round(Math.max(10 - y, Math.min(STAGE_H - 10 - h - y, dy))))
        },

    // the width the grip drags — the parent's where a child follows it, the
    // row's where a child flexes — is the one the screen's width control names,
    // kept in that control's range

    widthKnob(id: string) -> Knob? {
        return app.steps.find((s) => s.id == id)?.knobs.find((k) => k.name == "panelWidth" || k.name == "rowWidth") ?? null
        },
    widthOf(name: string) -> number { return name == "panelWidth" ? app.choices.value.panelWidth : app.choices.value.rowWidth },
    resizing: boolean = { app.widthKnob(app.stepId) != null },
    widthNow: number = { app.widthOf(app.widthKnob(app.stepId)?.name ?? "") },
    setWidth(w: number) {
        const k = widthKnob(stepId)
        if (k != null) choices.set([k.name], Math.round(Math.max(k.min ?? w, Math.min(k.max ?? w, w))))
        },

    // the spring screen's spring: `t`, carried toward 1 while open

    openT: number = 0,
    Spring [ attribute = openT, to = { app.choices.value.open ? 1 : 0 }, stiffness = 120, damping = 14 ],

    // the data screens' records, and the six labels the cast's pieces carry

    records: Records [ ] { { "rows": [
        { "id": 1, "label": "Design", "status": "doing" }, { "id": 2, "label": "Build", "status": "doing" },
        { "id": 3, "label": "Ship", "status": "done" }, { "id": 4, "label": "Test", "status": "done" } ] } },
    labels: string[] = ["Design", "Build", "Ship", "Test", "Plan", "Learn"],
    presses: number = 0,

    dragging: boolean = false,
    outlines: boolean = false,
    contentsOpen: boolean = false,

    // what this screen's stage does

    chipsLive: boolean = { app.step?.live != null },
    chipsToggle: boolean = { app.step?.live == "toggle" },
    dragKnob: boolean = { app.step?.drag ?? false },
    following: boolean = { app.dragging || app.stepId == "spring" },

    // ── the stage's pose

    director: Director [ ],
    scene: Scene = { app.director.scene(app.stepId) },
    cast: Dataset [ schema = Cast, contents = { { k: app.scene.k } } ],
    notesShown: Dataset [ contents = { { notes: app.leavingNotes() } } ],
    leavingNotes() -> Note[] {
        const cur = scene.notes, has = new Set(cur.map((n) => n.id))
        const before = prevStep != stepId ? director.raw(prevStep).notes : []
        return [...cur, ...before.filter((n) => !has.has(n.id)).map((n) => ({ ...n, gone: true }))]
        },
    wordsW: number = { app.stage.words.width },
    wordsH: number = { app.stage.words.height },

    // ── the code shown

    listing: Listing [ ],
    codeShown: Dataset [ schema = [ lines[]: CodeRow ],
        contents = { { lines: app.listing.merged(app.listing.lines(app.prevStep), app.listing.lines(app.stepId),
            app.listing.lines(app.order[app.index - 1] ?? "")) } } ],

    // ── the screen: the contents beside the page on a wide window; the lesson
    // — stage and code — as one card, the stage above the code where it is narrow

    wide: boolean = { app.width >= 1000 },
    stacked: boolean = { app.main.card.width < 820 },
    narrow: boolean = { app.main.foot.width < 520 },      // no room for the ticks
    compact: boolean = { app.main.foot.width < 720 },     // Next without the screen's title
    stage: Stage = { app.main.card.stageSide.room.stage },

    scrolls = none,
    layout: SimpleLayout [ axis = x, align = stretch ],

    side: View [ visible = { app.wide }, width = 280, scrolls = y,
        padding = [24, 12, 24, 12], accessibilityRole = navigation, accessibilityLabel = "Contents",
        fill = { provided("theme").railFill }, stroke = { [null, Stroke(1, provided("theme").railStrokeColor), null, null] },
        layout: SimpleLayout [ axis = y, spacing = 4 ],
        titleRow: View [ width = 100%, padding = [0, 4, 4, 12],
            layout: SimpleLayout [ axis = x, align = center ],
            Text [ flexes = true, fontSize = 17, fontWeight = semibold, text = "The Declare model" ],
            AppearanceSwitch [ dark = { app.isDark },
                commit(v: boolean) { app.themeMode = v ? "dark" : "light" }
                ]
            ],
        Text [ width = 100%, padding = [0, 12, 4, 12], fontSize = 13, textColor = { provided("theme").textMuted },
            text = "How Declare puts things on the screen, one point at a time." ],
        Text [ width = 100%, padding = [0, 12, 8, 12], fontSize = 12, textColor = { provided("theme").textFaint },
            text = "The stage animates each change so you can follow it; a program changes at once unless it moves its views." ],
        Contents [ ]
        ],

    // (stacked, the page is taller than the window, and scrolls)

    main: View [ flexes = true, padding = [28, 32, 32, 32], accessibilityRole = main, scrolls = { app.stacked ? "y" : "none" },
        layout: SimpleLayout [ axis = y, spacing = 18 ],

        // the screen's title and point; where the contents are hidden, a bar
        // that opens them and says where the reader is

        head: View [ width = 100%,
            layout: SimpleLayout [ axis = y, spacing = 8 ],
            bar: View [ visible = { !app.wide }, width = 100%,
                layout: SimpleLayout [ axis = x, spacing = 8, align = center ],
                ContentsButton [ press() { app.contentsOpen = true }
                    ],
                Text [ flexes = true, fontSize = 13, fontWeight = medium, textColor = { provided("theme").textMuted },
                    text = { app.whereIs(app.index) } ],
                AppearanceSwitch [ dark = { app.isDark },
                    commit(v: boolean) { app.themeMode = v ? "dark" : "light" }
                    ]
                ],
            Text [ width = 100%, accessibilityRole = heading, fontSize = { app.width < 600 ? 26 : 34 }, fontWeight = semibold,
                letterSpacing = -0.5, text = { app.step?.title ?? "" } ],

            // two lines held for the point, whatever it needs, so the lesson
            // below starts in the same place on every screen

            Text [ width = { Math.min(720, parent.width) }, height = { Math.max(50, this.contentHeight) }, fontSize = 18, textColor = { provided("theme").textMuted },
                text = { app.step?.point ?? "" } ]
            ],

        // the lesson: the stage, with what the reader can do to it along its
        // foot, beside the code. It takes the height the title and point leave,
        // which they hold the same on every screen, so its size follows the
        // window and nothing else: nothing in it moves as the screens change.
        // (Its edge is drawn over its contents, last, where they cannot cover it.)

        card: View [ width = 100%, flexes = { !app.stacked }, cornerRadius = 18, clip = true,
            fill = { provided("theme").cardFill },
            layout: ResponsiveLayout [ align = stretch, gap = 0, plan = { [
                ({ from: 820, flow: "row", share: ({ stageSide: 100 }) }),
                ({ from: 0, flow: "stack", share: ({ stageSide: 100, codeBox: 100 }) }) ] } ],

            // The stage side: above the stage, centred, what to do here and the
            // screen's controls; the stage; and below it, centred, the switch for
            // how the stage is drawn. Each row is held on every screen, so the
            // stage is the same size on all of them.

            stageSide: View [ accessibilityRole = region, accessibilityLabel = "The stage", fill = { provided("theme").stageFill },
                State [ applied = { app.stacked }, height = { this.width * 0.7 + 48 + app.target + 64 } ],
                layout: SimpleLayout [ axis = y ],

                // (a row of controls wider than the stage, where the window is
                // narrow, scrolls)

                top: View [ width = 100%, height = { app.target + 64 }, padding = [18, 12, 10, 12], datapath = { app.step },
                    layout: SimpleLayout [ axis = y, spacing = 10, align = center ],
                    Text [ maxLines = 1, fontSize = 16, fontWeight = medium,
                        textColor = { provided("theme").hintTextColor }, text = { :hint ?? "" } ],

                    // (centred by a spacer each side, which give their room up first)

                    controls: View [ width = 100%, scrolls = x, fontSize = 13,
                        layout: SimpleLayout [ axis = x, spacing = 8, align = center ],
                        Spacer [ ],
                        View [ datapath = :knobs[],
                            classFor = { ({ segmented: ChoiceSegments, slider: ChoiceSlider, toggle: ChoiceToggle, verb: RecordVerb })[:kind ?? "toggle"] ?? ChoiceToggle } ],
                        Spacer [ ]
                        ]
                    ],
                room: View [ width = 100%, flexes = true,
                    fit: number = { Math.max(0.3, Math.min((this.width - 32) / STAGE_W, this.height / STAGE_H, 1.4)) },
                    stage: Stage [ scale = { parent.fit }, pivotX = 0, pivotY = 0, x = center, y = center ]
                    ],

                // a quiet aid, not part of the lesson: small, and grey even when on

                foot: View [ width = 100%, height = 44,
                    theme = { app.isDark ? ({ ...SanFranciscoDark, ...TourDark, ...QuietDark, ...app.fingerSizes })
                        : ({ ...SanFrancisco, ...TourLight, ...QuietLight, ...app.fingerSizes }) },
                    boxesSwitch: Switch [ x = center, y = center, label = "Show boxes", fontSize = 12,
                        textColor = { provided("theme").textFaint }, checked = { app.outlines },
                        commit(v: boolean) { app.outlines = v }
                        ]
                    ]
                ],

            codeBox: View [ padding = [20, 8, 20, 0], scrolls = { app.stacked ? "both" : "y" },
                fill = { provided("theme").codeFill }, stroke = { [null, null, null, Stroke(1, provided("theme").cardStrokeColor)] },
                State [ applied = { app.stacked }, height = 260, stroke = { [Stroke(1, provided("theme").cardStrokeColor), null, null, null] } ],

                // as wide as the code beside the stage; as wide as the card below it

                lines: View [ width = 440, datapath = { app.codeShown.value },
                    State [ applied = { app.stacked }, width = { Math.max(440, parent.width - 8) } ],
                    layout: SimpleLayout [ axis = y ],
                    CodeLine [ datapath = :lines[] ]
                    ]
                ],
            edge: View [ ignoreLayout = true, width = 100%, height = 100%, cornerRadius = 18, pointerEvents = "none",
                stroke = { Stroke(1, provided("theme").cardStrokeColor) } ]
            ],

        // back, where the reader is, next

        foot: View [ width = 100%,
            layout: SimpleLayout [ axis = x, spacing = 20, align = center ],
            backLink: BackLink [ disabled = { app.index == 0 },
                press() { app.back() }
                ],
            Progress [ flexes = true ],
            nextButton: NextPill [ disabled = { app.index >= app.order.length - 1 },
                title = { app.steps[app.index + 1]?.title ?? "" },
                press() { app.next() }
                ]
            ]
        ],

    contentsSheet: Sheet [ edge = "start", accessibilityLabel = "Contents", shown = { app.contentsOpen && !app.wide },
        commit(open: boolean) { app.contentsOpen = open },
        Contents [ ]
        ]
    ]
